ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All direct and indirect shareholders, directors, legal representatives, and senior management of the investor must be screened against the following databases: (i) China's Ministry of Public Security and SAMR risk lists; (ii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List; (iii) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions list; (iv) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions list; (v) HKMA and Taiwan FSC AML/CFT watchlists. Screening must be updated within 24 hours prior to filing beneficial owner information under PBOC Order No. 3, and source of funds for the registered capital contribution must be documented. Any match triggers enhanced due diligence and a suspicious transaction report to the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Self-Service Declaration System (Name Registration Platform)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Chinese language mandatory; name structure: Administrative Division + Distinctive Name + Industry/Character + 'Co., Ltd.' For WFOE, the foreign investor's name must be transliterated phonetically into Chinese for the distinctive name. Four-tier naming convention applies: (1) country, (2) administrative district, (3) trade name, (4) organization type. English names are not permitted in the official registration except as reserved for international usage.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the SAMR Name Review Committee within 15 working days of receipt of the rejection notice. The appeal must be submitted through the National Enterprise Name Self-Service Declaration System, attaching a written explanation of the proposed name's non-conflict with existing names and compliance with Article 6 of the Measures for Enterprise Name Registration. If the SAMR maintains the rejection, the applicant may initiate a written reconsideration to the comprehensive enterprise registration authority at the provincial level, and finally seek judicial review under the Administrative Litigation Law of the PRC. Time limit and procedural documents are strictly construed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for the initial registration only if it is a registered physical address under a serviced office agreement and is not a mere post office box. However, for the dry bulk mineral ore trading industry (ISIC 4669), the municipal tax authority and commercial banks under AML KYC policy will reject a purely virtual or commercial-mailbox-only address because the company must present a lease contract, on-site business signs, and staff presence for invoice quota approval and bank account opening. A hybrid arrangement with a physical office room and shared meeting space is accepted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) physical signboard matching registered name; (2) lease agreement and rent payment records; (3) employee attendance and social insurance records; (4) accounting books and VAT invoice records; (5) actual business correspondence. Quantified risk: approximately 30% likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 18 months, driven by municipal tax invoice auditing and SAMR random sampling for mineral wholesale entities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Companies Act (the Companies Act), Articles 6, 7, 28, 98 to 113, and 128 to 156; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 3, 7 and 12; Act Governing Relations between the People of Taiwan and Mainland Area, Articles 72 and 73; Foreign Trade Act, Articles 15 and 20; Ministry of Economic Affairs Company Registration Directions; Fire Services Act; Occupational Safety and Health Act
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Company Registration Division, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (R.O.C.); Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs for foreign and Mainland investment approval
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application and Articles of Incorporation, filed on the MOEA Company Registration Online Platform
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Taiwan Companies Act for a general trading and brokerage company. However, the subscribers must fully subscribe and pay the stated capital before registration. The paid-in capital must be deposited into a dedicated paid-in capital settlement account at a Taiwanese bank, and a bank-issued certificate of paid-in capital must be filed with the Registrar. The capital may not be returned, withdrawn, or transferred out of the account prior to issuance of the Company Registration Certificate. The Investment Commission may impose a higher paid-in capital threshold or a proof-of-funds requirement at the time of foreign-investment approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF THE COMPANY. The directors of the Company, a Taiwan company limited by shares, convened at the first meeting of the Board of Directors on [DATE] at [TIME] at the proposed registered office. All directors were present and waived formal notice. The chairperson declared that a quorum existed and that the resolutions below were introduced, seconded, and unanimously adopted. A. SUBSCRIPTION AND PAID-IN CAPITAL: RESOLVED that the capital subscription schedule, as presented to the meeting, is hereby approved; that the subscriptions listed therein are accepted; and that each subscriber shall pay the full amount subscribed in cash into a dedicated paid-in capital settlement account to be opened by the Company at a bank approved by the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors are authorized to obtain a bank certificate of paid-in capital, to instruct the bank to release such funds only after the Company Registration Certificate is issued, and to take all steps necessary to verify that no subscriber capital is withdrawn, returned, or encumbered before completion of statutory registration. B. BANKING AUTHORITY: RESOLVED that [BANK NAME] is designated as the principal bank of the Company; that the Chairperson, the General Manager, and the Finance Controller, any two acting jointly, are authorized to open, operate, and close bank accounts, sign checks and drafts, accept remittances, negotiate letters of credit, execute loan and trade-finance instruments, and deliver banking indemnities in the ordinary course of business; and that banking mandate forms may be filed using any two of the aforementioned signatures. C. REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company shall be located at [ADDRESS]; that the Chairperson is authorized to execute or amend the lease, obtain landlord consent for business registration, and file the registered office address with the Department of Commerce and all relevant tax and regulatory authorities. D. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: RESOLVED that [NAME] is appointed Chairperson and statutory representative of the Company; [NAME] is appointed General Manager; [NAME] is appointed Company Secretary; and [NAME] is appointed Finance Controller. Each officer shall have all powers usual and customary to such office, shall hold office until the next general meeting or until replaced, and shall be responsible for implementing these resolutions and completing all corporate, tax, foreign trade, customs, labor, and environmental compliance filings. E. EXECUTION AUTHORITY: RESOLVED that the Chairperson, the General Manager, and the Company Secretary, any two acting together, are authorized individually and jointly to execute, notarize, file, and deliver any applications, declarations, certifications, powers of attorney, acknowledgments, and supplemental documents required to complete the incorporation, the opening of bank accounts, and the licensing and trade registration processes contemplated by these resolutions. UNANIMOUSLY ADOPTED on [DATE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Company Name Pre-Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; Department of Commerce via MOEA One-Stop Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the foreign-investment application and company name pre-review application through the MOEA One-Stop Internet Portal. The foreign investor must provide a corporate existence certificate, audited financial statements or a bank reference letter, a power of attorney, and a description of the proposed industrial mineral and sulfur brokerage scope. The Investment Commission and the Department of Commerce will review foreign ownership, admissible business scope under ISIC 4669 and NAICS 423520, and national security or trade policy restrictions. A favorable pre-review and approval letter are conditions precedent to bank account opening and final company registration; applicant should not remit or deposit subscribed capital before the approval letter is issued.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application Form
Certificate of incorporation and good standing of the investing company
Audited financial statements or bank reference for the ultimate investor
Proposed business scope referencing ISIC 4669 and NAICS 423520
Company name reservation application form
Power of attorney in favor of local representative
Identity documents of the nominated directors and responsible person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a query or suspension, submit the supplemental corporate and beneficial ownership records within the statutory correction period of thirty days. If the application is formally refused, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within thirty days after service of the decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Paid-in Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan District Court or authorized notary public; designated Taiwanese bank for paid-in capital certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the foreign-investment approval, convene the subscribers to adopt the Articles of Incorporation, elect the directors and supervisors, and approve the paid-in capital plan. The Articles must state the corporate name, purpose, legal scope, registered office location, aggregate share capital, class and par value of shares, and directors powers. The subscribers must sign the Articles and accompanying consents before a Taiwan notary public or district court clerk. Thereafter, open a temporary paid-in capital settlement account, receive the remitted foreign or Mainland funds under applicable foreign-exchange rules, and obtain a bank-issued certificate of paid-in capital dated no earlier than the statutory period before company registration.
required_dossiers: Investment Commission/MOEA approval letter
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of the subscribers subscription meeting
Notarized signature and seal registration forms
Bank paid-in capital certificate
Evidence of foreign currency remittance and exchange settlement
Power of attorney for notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or bank rejects a document for a technical defect, correct the signature blocks, recertify the Articles, and obtain a fresh paid-in capital certificate. The original foreign-investment approval remains valid if the cure is completed within its validity period; no new approval is required unless the ownership or capital amount changes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Registration Application with MOEA Department of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Registration Division, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (R.O.C.)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Company Establishment Registration Application together with the notarized Articles, subscription meeting minutes, shareholder list, bank capital certificate, foreign-investment approval, registered office proof, and director consents through the MOEA company registration platform or the regional commercial registration office. The Registrar will examine name compliance, share subscription, paid-in capital verification, registered office jurisdiction, and disqualification of directors. Pay the applicable registration fee and obtain the Company Registration Certificate issued by the Ministry. If the Registrar identifies missing or inconsistent documents, the applicant will receive a defect notice setting a cure deadline; correct all cited items before the deadline to preserve filing priority.
required_dossiers: Company Establishment Registration Application
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Subscription meeting minutes and shareholder list
Capital verification bank certificate
Foreign and/or Mainland investment approval license
Registered office lease and landlord consent
Director and responsible person consent forms
Name reservation certificate
Payment voucher for registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a defect notice, amend and re-file within the stated cure period. If a formal refusal is entered, file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within thirty days of service and resubmit the corrected application with all attachments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Foreign Trade, Customs, and Labor Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance; Bureau of Foreign Trade, MOEA; Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance; Bureau of Labor Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuing the Company Registration Certificate, register the Company with the National Taxation Bureau for tax identification and uniform invoice number, enabling issuance of VAT invoices and withholding statements. If the Company will execute principal-to-principal trades in granular elemental sulfur, apply for Foreign Trade Registration under the Foreign Trade Act, register as an import/export trader with the Customs Administration, and obtain customs authentication. The Company must also file labor insurance, health insurance, and labor pension registrations with the Bureau of Labor Insurance. The bank account authority resolution is delivered to the bank to activate the account and any requested letter-of-credit or electronic banking capabilities.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Notarized Articles and company seal card
National Taxation Bureau Uniform Invoice/Tax Registration Application
Foreign Trade Registration application under the Foreign Trade Act
Customs Administration Import/Export Registration application
Labor insurance, health insurance, and pension employer forms
Bank account mandate and signature cards
Responsible person national ID or passport
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax or foreign-trade registration is queried, cure the missing document at the relevant single-service window. Voluntary correction before a formal audit or investigation can reduce or eliminate penalties under the Tax Collection Act and Foreign Trade Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activation of Banking, Trade Financing, and Licensing Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Environment, Taiwan (R.O.C.); Department of Commerce, MOEA; designated bank; shipping and customs agents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before the first transaction, verify that no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing facility will be operated by the Company, and file a no-physical-facility declaration with the Department of Commerce and the local Ministry of Environment office. Confirm that no Environmental Impact Assessment and no Civil Defense fire permit are required for the administrative brokerage office. If the Company arranges ocean carriage or brokerage of bulk granular sulfur, ensure shippers, carriers, and vessels hold applicable IMO Dangerous Goods documentation for sulfur as a Class 4.1 solid and meet Taiwan port and customs requirements. Execute internal procedures for Letter of Credit settlement, sanctions screening, and AML/KYC compliance with the issuing and negotiating banks.
required_dossiers: No physical facility declaration
Dangerous Goods Declaration and IMO Class 4.1 documentation for sulfur cargoes
Draft Letter of Credit and SWIFT LC instructions
AML/KYC documentation for the corporate bank account
P&I and marine cargo insurance certificates if applicable
Trade compliance manual and sanctions screening policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank flags AML, KYC, or letter-of-credit issues, provide updated beneficial-ownership forms and corrected LC drafts. If customs or port authorities query dangerous-goods documentation, issue a corrected Dangerous Goods Declaration and coordinate with the carrier to meet the twenty-four-hour shipment deadline; consequential delays are mitigated by early broker-caused submission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable at formation; if the Company later adds warehousing or sulfur handling, the competent authority will be the Ministry of Environment, Taiwan (R.O.C.) and the local urban-planning and civil-defense authorities; foreign trade registration remains with the Bureau of Foreign Trade, MOEA.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — the Company is engaged in dry-bulk marine transport brokerage and wholesale mineral brokerage only, with no manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing facility. No industrial operating permit or manufacturing license is required. The Company must, however, maintain Foreign Trade Registration and Customs Import/Export Registration if it executes principal-to-principal trades in granular elemental sulfur.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Taiwan (R.O.C.), successor to the Environmental Protection Administration
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not applicable — Exempt from Environmental Impact Assessment for a pure trading and brokerage office. If a future sulfur warehouse, transfer station, or processing operation is proposed, the project will require a Category B or site-specific environmental review under Article 5 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act before construction or operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable quantitative thresholds for a pure brokerage office because no industrial wastewater, VOC source, or hazardous process waste is generated. Should future physical sulfur handling occur, the operator must comply with the Taiwan Air Pollution Control Act emission standards, manage sulfur as UN 1350 Class 4.1 dangerous goods, and meet applicable effluent standards for any industrial wastewater, including chemical oxygen demand limits not exceeding typical general-industry standards of 100 mg/L where discharge is to a sanitary sewer or water body; hazardous waste must be manifested and disposed of by an approved handler.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable — no Civil Defense fire permit or fire-safety certification is required for a dry-bulk trading and brokerage head-office that operates only an administrative office. If the Company leases commercial office premises, the tenant and landlord must comply with the Fire Services Act self-protection and fire-safety management obligations for the premises, and the Company must satisfy the Occupational Safety and Health Act general workplace duties covering emergency exits, first-aid, and electrical safety; no manufacturing-site structural-load approval is triggered.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); primary digital portal is the National Unified Standard e-Tax Platform at https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn with identity authentication at https://tpass.chinatax.gov.cn; export-related records are exchanged with the General Administration of Customs (GACC) through the China International Trade Single Window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The foreign parent incorporates the WFOE as a limited liability company with the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) under the Foreign Investment Law, obtaining the Business License containing the statutory 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). Step 2: Under the 'one license, one code' and 'multi-license integration' reforms, the USCC is automatically recognized by the STA as the enterprise taxpayer identification number (TIN) and VAT registration number; no separate tax registration application is required for the entity. Step 3: Within 30 days of license issuance, the WFOE must complete tax-registration information confirmation on the e-Tax platform, file its bank account particulars, submit its accounting system and bookkeeping filings, apply for invoice quota, and confirm general VAT taxpayer status once annual taxable sales reach or exceed the statutory threshold. Step 4: Where the WFOE pays dividends, interest, royalties, or fees to non-resident shareholders or counterparties, it must register as a withholding agent; the WFOE itself is a PRC tax resident, so no separate branch or permanent-establishment registration applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: China does not offer US-style check-the-box elections or hybrid mismatch elections. Statutory elections and filings relevant to a trading WFOE: (1) a small-scale VAT taxpayer with annual taxable sales not exceeding RMB 5 million may elect to register as a general VAT taxpayer to claim input VAT credits, with an irrevocable 12-month lock-in; (2) a qualifying small low-profit enterprise may elect to apply the preferential corporate income tax effective rate (5% for taxable income up to RMB 3 million); (3) export VAT treatment is mandatory and method is not elective - trading enterprises use the exemption-and-refund method, while production enterprises use the exemption-credit-refund method; (4) tax treaty relief on cross-border income is claimed through a statutory treaty-benefit application.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), a statutory sub-ministry authority executing the foreign-exchange administration powers of the People's Bank of China (PBOC). For the Taiwan leg, the PBOC also coordinates with the Bank of China Taipei Branch, which acts as the designated RMB clearing bank for Taiwan under the Cross-Strait Financial Cooperation Agreement of 2009, and with the Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) for inter-bank correspondence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Current account: fully convertible in practice for goods, services, and routine profit remittances since China's acceptance of IMF Article VIII obligations (effective December 1996). A WFOE may wire distributable dividends to its Taiwan shareholder after: (i) the annual statutory audit, (ii) final settlement of Corporate Income Tax via the annual reconciliation return (汇算清缴) with payment of any tax due, and (iii) submission to the remitting bank of the audited balance sheet, income statement, board dividend resolution, and the tax-payment certificate (完税证明). The bank applies an authenticity review only; there is no pre-approval quota and no SAFE license step. Capital account: restricted. Registered-capital injections require prior SAFE FDI registration; the imported capital can then be used for genuine operating purposes under the 'willful settlement' (意愿结汇) policy, but converted RMB earmarked for future use must remain in a dedicated settlement-pending account (结汇待支付账户). Shareholder loans, buyback of equity, and dissolution-remittance are separate capital items requiring either SAFE registration or approval. Cross-strait RMB: RMB remittances between the WFOE and Taiwan counterparties are permitted via the cross-strait RMB clearing mechanism without special quota, provided the underlying trade or investment documents evidence genuine transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Repatriation: all export proceeds from granular elemental sulfur (HS 2503.00) must be credited to the WFOE's current-account foreign-exchange account at a licensed SAFE bank onshore; offshore retention requires SAFE case-by-case approval. Collection timeline: proceeds should be collected within 90 calendar days from the date of the customs export declaration; collections beyond 90 days must be reported as delayed collection (延期收款) in the SAFE Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring Platform within 30 days of actual receipt, and systematic delays will trigger an aggregate trade-inspection (总量核查) downgrade. Conversion: since July 2012 the mandatory surrender ratio is zero - the WFOE may retain 100% of export receipts in USD or convert to RMB at its discretion by onshore spot settlement; the SAFE 2019 reform (Public Notice [2019] No.28) further removed the former foreign-exchange account retention ceiling; A-class trade-status enterprises are nevertheless expected to demonstrate an annual export-receipt collection coverage ratio generally at or above 90% by customs value, and invoicing, customs declarations, and receipts must be reconcilable in the monitoring platform.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, including certified financial statements when the statutory audit threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 of the calendar year following the taxable year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within five months after the close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax (20% if filed after commencement of a tax investigation); late payment surcharge of 1% per two days of delinquency, capped at 15%; unresolved delinquency may lead to compulsory distraint and administrative strike-off of the registered company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting with presentation and approval of the annual business report, financial statements, and profit appropriation or loss recognition proposal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders; meeting minutes and financial reports must be retained in the statutory minute book and made available to the competent authority upon inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the close of the fiscal year, ordinarily by June 30 for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors are subject to administrative fines under the Taiwan Company Act for failure to convene the annual meeting; continued default may trigger a Ministry of Economic Affairs investigation and compulsory dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Operation Survey Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the filing period set by the Investment Commission, typically by the end of February following the reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or false filing is subject to corrective orders and administrative penalties; recurrent noncompliance may suspend or revoke outstanding foreign-investment approvals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholding and Non-Withholding Statement Filing for salaries, dividends, royalties, and other Taiwan-sourced payments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before January 31 of the calendar year following the year in which the payments were made
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under Article 114 of the Income Tax Act for failure to file or for erroneous filing; the withholding agent additionally remains liable for the withheld tax plus a delinquency surcharge, with compulsory collection for sustained default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Change Registrations and Maintenance of Statutory Registers for directors, shareholders, registered office, and articles of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after each triggering corporate event; register accuracy is verified during annual audit review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of NT$10,000 to NT$50,000 for registration violations; a company that never commences business or discontinues operations for more than six months may be administratively dissolved and struck off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A certified public accountant audit is mandatory if paid-in capital reaches NT$30 million (approximately US$1.0 million) or more, if the entity is a public or Financial Supervisory Commission-regulated enterprise, or if the Ministry of Economic Affairs so requires under the Company Act; foreign-owned trading entities above these thresholds must file audited financial statements with the annual tax return.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies apply Taiwan IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission; non-public enterprises apply the Business Entity Accounting Standards under the Commercial Accounting Act, which are aligned with IFRS for SMEs, and may elect full IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan's beneficial-owner confirmation requires annual updating and an additional update within 15 days of any change in the particulars of directors, supervisors, managers, or shareholders holding 10% or more; transfer of shares in the Taiwan entity must be posted to the Register of Members and reflected in the annual beneficial-owner confirmation filed on the Ministry of Economic Affairs platform, and material omissions or false filings incur fines and may invalidate corporate registration.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$300-US$1,200 per annum for a registered office address and corporate secretarial or agent services, varying by location and service scope.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,000-US$15,000 per annum for a Taiwan CPA audit of a small-to-mid-size bulk mineral trading entity, varying with turnover, transaction volume, and cross-border documentation complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% for a standard resident enterprise and wholly foreign-owned enterprise in mainland China.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small low-profit enterprises may qualify for reduced effective rates subject to annual revenue, employee, and asset thresholds. Qualified high and new technology enterprises may apply a 15% rate. Certain encouraged industries and regions may receive preferential rates, tax holidays, or additional deductions. Research and development expenses may qualify for an additional super-deduction, subject to statutory conditions and documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return for Resident Enterprises, including the main form and schedules, filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax bureau. Quarterly provisional Enterprise Income Tax Return is also filed electronically.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly provisional filing and annual final filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional returns are generally due within 15 days after the end of each quarter. The annual return and tax reconciliation are generally due within five months after the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the normal annual deadline is 31 May of the following year, subject to official holiday extensions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Main Form: taxpayer identification and enterprise classification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the unified social credit code, legal name, registered address, tax residence status, accounting system, applicable tax rate, and enterprise classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A mainland China WFOE is normally a resident enterprise for China Enterprise Income Tax purposes. Do not report it as a non-resident enterprise merely because its shareholders are foreign.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report revenue from sulfur and mineral trading, brokerage commissions, marine transport-related services, agency services, and other operating activities on an accrual basis under China tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident enterprise reports China-source income attributable to its China establishment or China-source income subject to withholding, as applicable. Allocate revenue between the China establishment and offshore activities using supportable records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Main Form: operating costs and expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report cost of goods sold, freight, port charges, insurance, brokerage costs, employee costs, depreciation, financing costs, and other deductible expenses supported by valid invoices and commercial evidence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses of a non-resident enterprise must be directly connected with China-source income or the China establishment and must satisfy statutory documentation and deductibility requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax Adjustment Schedule: non-deductible and tax-adjustment items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjust accounting profit for non-deductible expenses, excess entertainment expenses, unsupported provisions, non-compliant depreciation, related-party adjustments, donations exceeding limits, and other book-tax differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude expenses unrelated to China-source income. Apply withholding-tax rules instead of resident-enterprise deductions where the payment is made to an offshore recipient without a China establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose related-party purchases, sales, services, financing, royalties, guarantees, and other transactions, together with pricing, transaction type, counterparty jurisdiction, and transfer-pricing documentation status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose transactions between the WFOE and foreign shareholders, affiliates, procurement entities, financing entities, and logistics or trading affiliates. Cross-border related-party transactions must be consistent with customs, foreign-exchange, VAT, and transfer-pricing records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim eligible prior-year tax losses within the statutory carryforward period, subject to continuity, documentation, and applicable industry or restructuring restrictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident enterprise generally cannot use losses of a foreign head office against China-source income unless specifically permitted under the applicable China tax rules and establishment accounting requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax Credit Schedule: foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim qualifying foreign income tax credits within the applicable limitation, supported by foreign tax payment certificates and income allocation schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A China resident WFOE may claim qualifying foreign tax credits on foreign-source income subject to statutory limits. A non-resident enterprise generally claims relief under the applicable treaty or withholding mechanism rather than through a broad resident-company credit computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile provisional payments, annual tax payable, tax credits, tax incentives, withholding tax, and the final balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, and service fees is separately reported and not improperly netted against Enterprise Income Tax of the WFOE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may trigger a statutory administrative fine, commonly up to RMB 2,000 and, for serious cases, RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000. Late payment generally incurs a surcharge of 0.05% of unpaid tax per day, calculated from the day after the statutory payment deadline. Tax authorities may impose additional penalties for inaccurate reporting, failure to maintain records, or failure to submit related-party information. Tax evasion may result in recovery of tax, surcharge, administrative fines, and criminal prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Related-Party Transactions Annual Reporting Form, submitted with the annual Enterprise Income Tax filing through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax bureau.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due together with the annual Enterprise Income Tax return within five months after the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify each related party, jurisdiction, relationship type, ownership percentage, and transaction category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include foreign parent companies, affiliates, beneficial owners, treasury companies, procurement hubs, logistics affiliates, and entities under common control.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tangible goods, services, financing, intangible property, guarantees, and other related-party transaction values.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile transaction totals to the general ledger, customs declarations, VAT returns, foreign-exchange settlement records, and intercompany agreements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the selected arm's-length method, tested party, profit-level indicator, comparable analysis, and relevant financial results.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the method consistently with the Local File and ensure that the tested party has the functions, assets, and risk profile described in the documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Master File and Local File status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate whether documentation thresholds are met, whether a Master File or Local File is prepared, and whether any exemption is relied upon.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An exemption from preparing a document does not eliminate the arm's-length requirement or the obligation to provide information during an audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to submit related-party reporting forms or submission of materially inaccurate information may result in administrative fines and adverse transfer-pricing adjustments. Failure to provide documentation may cause an adjustment, a higher deemed interest rate on underpaid tax, and reduced access to simplified dispute procedures.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid by a mainland China resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise, subject to applicable treaty relief, beneficial-ownership requirements, and any competent-authority or administrative procedures.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide evidence of tax residence, beneficial ownership, ownership and holding-period information, corporate documents, payment contracts, and any other documents required by the State Taxation Administration. Treaty relief is generally implemented through a withholding-agent assessment and documentation process, with certain cases requiring tax filing, record-filing, or competent-authority approval. The payer must verify treaty eligibility, retain supporting records, calculate the reduced rate correctly, withhold and remit tax, and report the payment. The Taiwan jurisdiction identifier creates a material legal classification issue: mainland China and Taiwan do not operate as an ordinary bilateral income-tax treaty pair for routine WFOE dividend relief. A Taiwan tax residence certificate should not be assumed to provide mainland China treaty relief without specific confirmation from the relevant tax authorities.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The standard mainland China withholding rate is generally 10% for interest and royalties paid to a non-resident enterprise, subject to statutory exclusions and treaty relief. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and may be lower. Royalties may also trigger VAT and surcharge obligations. Interest payments must be tested for thin-capitalization, deductibility, beneficial-ownership, withholding, foreign-exchange, and treaty anti-abuse requirements. Payments for services must be classified separately because China-source service income may create withholding, VAT, permanent-establishment, and enterprise-income-tax exposure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File thresholds generally include annual related-party tangible-asset transactions exceeding RMB 200 million, financial-asset transactions exceeding RMB 100 million, intangible-asset transactions exceeding RMB 100 million, or other related-party transactions exceeding RMB 40 million. A Master File is generally required where the China entity belongs to a multinational group with consolidated annual revenue of at least RMB 5 billion and specified cross-border related-party transactions or other prescribed conditions exist. Thresholds and exemptions must be tested for the relevant fiscal year and transaction category.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not operate a separate regime universally titled Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Substance is enforced through the Enterprise Income Tax Law, beneficial-ownership rules, general anti-avoidance rules, permanent-establishment principles, controlled foreign company rules, thin-capitalization rules, treaty anti-abuse standards, and transfer-pricing provisions. A company must demonstrate real functions, personnel, premises, assets, decision-making, commercial purpose, and risk control. A conduit company lacking substantive ownership or business activity may be denied treaty benefits and may face tax reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Jurisdictional misclassification and unauthorized business scope
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Taiwan tax jurisdiction code for a mainland China WFOE, or conducting mineral trading, brokerage, marine transport, or agency activities outside the registered business scope or without required approvals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, loss of preferential treatment, administrative fines, business-scope correction orders, suspension, license revocation, and possible confiscation of unlawful income. Transactions may also create customs, VAT, foreign-exchange, and regulatory liabilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face civil liability for losses, administrative sanctions, restrictions on serving as responsible persons, and criminal liability where the conduct involves fraud, illegal business operations, smuggling, or intentional tax evasion. Personal travel restrictions may be imposed through judicial enforcement for unpaid obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and false tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, fabricating costs, understating trading margins, using false invoices, creating sham intercompany charges, omitting offshore-related-party transactions, or claiming unsupported deductions or losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid tax, 0.05% daily late-payment surcharge, and administrative fines generally ranging from 50% to 500% of the evaded tax. Serious cases may be referred for criminal prosecution under the Criminal Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors, legal representatives, finance managers, and other directly responsible persons may face fines and imprisonment. Tax crimes can result in civil restitution, asset preservation, restrictions on consumption, and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing, purchasing, transferring, or using fabricated or fraudulently obtained VAT special invoices to inflate input credits, reduce taxable income, or support fictitious mineral transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Input-tax denial, tax recovery, confiscation, substantial fines, invoice-related sanctions, and criminal penalties that may include long-term imprisonment depending on the amount and circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, legal representatives, finance officers, and employees who knowingly participate may be criminally liable independently of the company's limited liability. Civil restitution, asset seizure, professional restrictions, and travel controls may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length prices for sulfur purchases, resale transactions, royalties, management fees, freight, financing, guarantees, or procurement services to shift profits outside China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Special tax adjustment, additional tax, late-payment interest calculated under the special adjustment rules, possible deemed withholding, and penalties for failure to provide reliable Local File, Master File, or related-party reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face administrative and civil consequences for deliberate misstatement or breach of fiduciary duties. Criminal exposure arises where transfer-pricing manipulation is part of tax evasion, invoice fraud, bribery, or fraudulent foreign-exchange activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, or royalties through a conduit entity in Taiwan or another jurisdiction that lacks substantive ownership, commercial purpose, personnel, assets, or control over the income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, withholding at the full domestic rate, recovery of underwithheld tax, late-payment surcharge, and anti-avoidance reassessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and tax officers may face liability for knowingly submitting false residence or beneficial-ownership evidence. Fraudulent documentation may lead to criminal prosecution and enforcement against personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal profit repatriation and foreign-exchange violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable accounting profits, statutory reserve allocations, audited accounts, tax clearance, or required foreign-exchange and banking documentation; using sham loans, inflated service fees, or fictitious imports to transfer funds offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Dividend reversal, tax recovery, foreign-exchange penalties, confiscation of unlawful gains, bank-account restrictions, and possible criminal liability for serious illegal foreign-exchange operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be required to restore improperly distributed funds and compensate the company or creditors. Serious cases may result in imprisonment, travel restrictions, disqualification from corporate office, and enforcement against personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-money laundering and trade-based money laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using circular trade, over-invoicing or under-invoicing of sulfur cargoes, unexplained third-party payments, opaque beneficial owners, forged bills of lading, unusual letters of credit, or accounts unrelated to the contractual counterparty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transaction rejection, enhanced due diligence, account freezing, suspicious-transaction reporting, administrative penalties, confiscation, and criminal prosecution for money laundering or predicate offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance personnel may face criminal liability if they knowingly facilitate laundering or conceal criminal proceeds. Civil restitution, asset seizure, travel bans, and imprisonment may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs, commodity-origin, sanctions, and controlled-trade violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misdeclaring sulfur classification, quantity, value, origin, end use, or consignee; falsifying shipping documents; or dealing with sanctioned entities, restricted ports, or prohibited counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs reassessment, confiscation, fines, cargo seizure, import or export suspension, license consequences, and criminal prosecution for smuggling or other customs offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives and responsible officers may incur criminal liability for intentional customs fraud or sanctions evasion, including imprisonment, fines, asset confiscation, civil restitution, and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Permanent establishment and unauthorized offshore activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Allowing foreign affiliates or personnel to habitually negotiate or conclude contracts in China, maintain dependent agents, control inventory, or conduct core trading functions without proper registration, tax reporting, or allocation of profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Enterprise Income Tax, VAT, withholding, interest, penalties, and possible retroactive tax registration or establishment recognition.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for unpaid corporate taxes caused by deliberate avoidance and personal sanctions where the conduct involves concealment, false filings, or obstruction of tax inspection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to preserve accounting and tax evidence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain contracts, invoices, customs declarations, bills of lading, inspection certificates, inventory records, bank confirmations, transfer-pricing analyses, and proof of beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Expense disallowance, deemed-profit assessment, denial of treaty relief, administrative fines, adverse evidentiary presumptions, and tax adjustment based on available information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and finance officers may be sanctioned for obstruction, destruction of records, or intentional non-compliance. Criminal liability may arise where document destruction conceals tax evasion, fraud, or money laundering.
